thread:
jamie: Heads up — seeing a cluster of intermittent Xid errors on A40s in rack-18. Started ~19:02 UTC, spread across pod-b and pod-d. No obvious memory pressure.
lee: saw the alerts, linked to two p2 workers. Any ECC spikes? :eyes:
sara: ECC corrected counts jumped on 3 GPUs in node-18-03 around the same time. dmesg shows repeated nv_peer_mem warnings.
jamie: pasting small log excerpt:

```
[1795123408.123] nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: Xid (65:16) 0x00000005
[1795123410.456] nv_peer_mem: peer memory op failed: -111
[1795123422.789] NVRM: Xid (13:60) 0x0000000e
```

matt: Xid 65/13 pattern tends to be PCIe fabric or driver-level; but we've also seen it with failing frontplane connectors on A40s.
anya: any recent firmware updates or BIOS knobs rolled?
lee: no scheduled fw in that rack. We did a host kernel bump on 1795123000 but only on pod-a nodes, not these.
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-179512 — "A40 rack-18 intermittent Xid cascade". Pager duty notified.
sara: quick triage status: node-18-03 and node-18-07 show continuous small ECC_Corrected delta + NV peer mem flaps. Node-18-02 shows one-off Xid and then recovered.
jamie: Plan: 1) drain node-18-03 and reprovision workload to pod markers 2) run nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.ecc.corrected_count,temperature.gpu --format=csv -l 1 for a few minutes 3) swap to spare slot / reseat frontplane cables 
sara: agreed. I'll start drain now. mtt in the queue will shift.
matt: also capture PCI topology: lspci -vvv on the nodes before reseat. If it's link flapping it should show AER errors.
anya: tagging hw-eng for possible RMA if reseat doesn't hold: @hw-eng.
lee: after drain: node-18-03 shows continued Xid on GPU 1 even with low utilization. Reseated frontplane cable and rebooted — Xid rate dropped to near-zero for 20m.
jamie: good sign. But node-18-07 still intermittent. We suspect either a bad cable or bad card batch. Any serial numbers?
sara: pulling serials: GPU 1 SN: A40-Z7F-0193, GPU 2 SN: A40-Z7F-0194, node-18-07 GPU 1 SN: A40-Z7F-0247. 0193 and 0247 share same vendor lot prefix Z7F.
matt: that correlates with last quarter's procurement lot (PO-2025-43). We flagged a small fraction then but it wasn't actionable.
ops-bot: Note: Running rolling replacement schedule may affect available capacity for scheduled training runs. Compute-scheduler notified of capacity drop.
anya: RCA draft (initial): root cause likely marginal frontplane connector / flaky A40 lot Z7F causing intermittent PCIe peer ops to fail under certain thermal cycles. Contributing factors: no proactive telemetry for frontplane AER counters, and host kernel didn't surface link flaps to our alerting.
lee: mitigation done: replaced cable for node-18-03, swapped GPU 1 in node-18-07 to spare, monitoring 2h.
jamie: next steps: 1) inventory PO-2025-43 serials across fleet and tag at-risk nodes 2) add AER/link-flap metric to infra exporter (kernel pcie_aer_count) 3) update runbook: drain -> reseat -> reseat cable -> replace card -> RMA 4) coordinate with procurement for extended warranty on lot Z7F
sara: I'll open a ticket to inventory serials and annotate nodes with tag "hw-risk:Z7F".
matt: I'll pick up the exporter PR for AER counters and add alert threshold: >2 link flaps / 10m triggers auto-drain.
anya: I'll touch base with vendor and initiate RMA for 2 cards if we get recurrence after reseat; keep RMA scope to serials with >1 Xid in 24h.
jamie: timeline: aim to finish inventory and PR by EOD tomorrow. If more than 5 nodes affected we escalate to exec ops.
lee: retrospective note: add a small hardware check to on-boarding health scan (check frontplane seating torque and cable strain).
sara: closing notes: no data loss, workloads failed over to spare capacity, tail latency spiked for some batch jobs ~3-4m during drain.
jamie: thanks everyone. I'll convert this thread into a short postmortem draft and attach logs. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Reminder: Tag incident INC-2026-179512 as "postmortem-required" if cause confirms hardware batch.
